Simulate TITE-BOIN12 Trials

Source: R/tite_boin12_simulate.R
tite_boin12_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of the TITE-BOIN12 design of Zhou et al. (2022), the time-to-event version of BOIN12 in which patients arrive over time, the DLT and the response are assessed over windows and the decisions use the outcomes still pending through the approximated likelihood. Return the patients, DLTs and responses at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_tite_boin12.

Usage

tite_boin12_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  window,
  accrual_rate,
  resp_window = window,
  accrual = c("uniform", "exponential", "fixed"),
  event_time = c("weibull", "uniform"),
  late_fraction = 0.5,
  resp_late_fraction = 0.5,
  min_completed_share = 0.5,
  pending_estimate = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  n_star = 6,
  n_explore = 9,
  tie_break = c("higher", "random"),
  no_candidate = c("nearest", "stop"),
  explore_from = c("any", "admissible"),
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, called phi_T by Lin et al. (2020). It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a dose and of the MTD that bounds the OBD. Lin et al. recommend a value slightly above the target of a design that only considers toxicity, for example 0.35 instead of 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E. Note that this is a lower limit, as in sim_bf_boin_et, whereas the target_resp of sim_boin_et is a target.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose.

p_resp

Numeric vector. True response probability at each dose.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

window

Numeric scalar. Length of the DLT assessment window.

accrual_rate

Numeric scalar. Average number of patients arriving per unit of time, in the same unit as window.

resp_window

Numeric scalar. Length of the response assessment window. Defaults to window.

accrual

Character scalar. Distribution of the times between arrivals: "uniform" (the default) on (0, 2 / accrual_rate), "exponential" for a Poisson process, or "fixed" for arrivals exactly 1 / accrual_rate apart.

event_time

Character scalar. Distribution of the times to DLT and to response: "weibull" (the default), with the share of the events in the second half of the window set by late_fraction and resp_late_fraction, or "uniform" over the window. With "weibull" the probabilities must be below 1.

late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Share of the DLTs that occur in the second half of the DLT window under the Weibull distribution. Defaults to 0.5.

resp_late_fraction

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. The same for the responses. Defaults to 0.5.

min_completed_share

Numeric scalar from 0 to 1. Share of the patients at the current dose who must have finished both assessments before the next decision; the decision, and the accrual, wait until then. Defaults to 0.5, the rule of Zhou et al. (2022), who suspend the accrual when more than half of the patients at the current dose have a pending outcome. With 1 every decision waits for all the outcomes, as in BOIN12.

pending_estimate

Character scalar. Value that replaces a pending outcome Y in the quasi-binomial likelihood: "conditional" (the default), the probability of the event given that it has not occurred during the time followed, pi_hat * (1 - w) / (1 - pi_hat * w), with w the fraction of the window followed, as in Equation (11) of Zhou et al. (2022); or "marginal", the estimate pi_hat itself, which reproduces the desirabilities of Table S.3 of their Supplement. See Details.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level of the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. Number of patients at the current dose that ends the trial when the next cohort would stay there (see n_earlystop_rule). Defaults to NULL, which runs every trial to the maximum sample size, as in Lin et al. (2020).

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar. "with_stay" (the default) ends the trial at n_earlystop only when the next cohort would stay at the current dose, as in the example of Zhou et al. (2022); "simple" ends it in any case.

p_saf, p_tox

Numeric scalars or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic and lowest deemed overly toxic, which give the BOIN boundaries. Default to 0.6 * target and 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both. The utility of a response without DLT is 100 and that of a DLT without response is 0. Default to 40 and 60, the example of Lin et al. (2020).

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. The utility benchmark is benchmark_weight * u_low + (1 - benchmark_weight) * 100, where u_low is the expected utility of a dose whose DLT and response probabilities are target and target_resp, the two outcomes being independent. Defaults to 0.5, the benchmark of Lin et al. (2020); Lu et al. (2025) use 0.6.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a dose divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_star

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current dose and a DLT rate between lambda_e and lambda_d, the next dose is chosen from the current dose and the dose below. Defaults to 6.

n_explore

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current dose, a DLT rate below lambda_d and an untried admissible dose above, the next cohort goes to that dose. Defaults to 9.

tie_break

Character scalar. Choice among the doses of equal desirability: "higher" (the default) takes the highest of them, the rule of the BOIN12 software according to the 'escalation' package; "random" takes one of them at random, as stated in Table S2 of the Supplement of Lin et al. (2020). See Details.

no_candidate

Character scalar. What happens when none of the doses allowed for the next cohort is admissible: "nearest" (the default) goes to the admissible dose nearest to the current one; "stop" ends the trial without an OBD. See Details.

explore_from

Character scalar. Doses from which the exploration rule (see n_explore) escalates: "any" (the default) from any dose, as in the 'escalation' package; "admissible" only from an admissible dose, as the results published by Lin et al. (2020) indicate. See Details.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type; with "copula" it also links the time to DLT and the time to response. Defaults to 0.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) links the two outcomes by a Gaussian copula with correlation resp_cor, the bivariate normal model of Lin et al. (2020); "binary" sets the correlation of the two binary outcomes, as in boin_et_simulate.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin12_trials, as returned by boin12_simulate, with design set to "TITE-BOIN12" and one more component

duration

Numeric vector of the duration of each trial: the time at which every patient has finished both assessments, or the time of the decision that stopped the trial because no dose was admissible or, with no_candidate = "stop", because no dose allowed for the next cohort was admissible.

The DLTs and responses are the final outcomes of all the patients.

Details

The first patient of a cohort arrives at the time of the previous decision, and the next decision is due when the next patient arrives. While fewer than a share min_completed_share of the patients at the current dose have finished both assessments, the decision waits for the next assessment to end. After the last cohort, and when the trial stops because n_earlystop is reached, the trial waits until every patient has finished both assessments, and the OBD is selected from the complete data, as in the example of Zhou et al. (2022).

At a decision, an outcome is observed once its event has occurred or its window has ended, and pending otherwise. For each dose, with w the fraction of the window followed by a pending patient, the DLT probability is estimated by pi_hat = DLTs observed / (DLTs observed + patients who completed the window without DLT + sum of w) (Equation 14 of the Supplement), and the response probability in the same way. The quasi-events of BOIN12 count each patient with a pending outcome by the expected utility, the pending outcome being replaced as set by pending_estimate and the two outcomes taken as independent for this purpose only. The desirability is that of BOIN12 with these quasi-events and the number of patients treated, and the rules of boin12_simulate are applied with pi_hat of the DLTs as the DLT rate of the current dose. With every outcome observed, these are exactly the quantities of BOIN12, so that min_completed_share = 1 with accrual = "fixed" gives the trials of boin12_simulate with the same seed.

Two points are not settled by Zhou et al. (2022) and are decided here as follows. Equation (11) replaces a pending outcome by its conditional expectation, but the desirabilities of their Table S.3 follow from pi_hat itself; both are offered by pending_estimate. The admissibility of a dose, which they update at every decision, uses the posterior of the approximated likelihood, Beta(1 + DLTs observed, 1 + patients who completed the window without DLT + sum of w), and the same for the responses, so that a response that is merely late does not exclude a dose. TITE-BOIN-ET (tite_boin_et_simulate) instead counts the pending patients as patients without the event, as the 'boinet' package does.

Each patient draws two uniform variates as in boin12_simulate; the time to DLT and the time to response are quantiles of their distributions at these variates, so that a DLT and a response occur within their windows with the probabilities p_true and p_resp. The times between arrivals draw further variates unless accrual = "fixed", and with tie_break = "random" a decision among tied doses draws one more variate after those of the cohort, as in boin12_simulate.

References

Zhou, Y., Lin, R., Lee, J. J., Li, D., Wang, L., Li, R. and Yuan, Y. (2022). TITE-BOIN12: A Bayesian phase I/II trial design to find the optimal biological dose with late-onset toxicity and efficacy. Statistics in Medicine, 41(11), 1918-1931. doi:10.1002/sim.9337

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

See also

sim_tite_boin12, boin12_simulate, boin12_select_obd

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Zhou et al. (2022), windows of 45 and 60 days and three
# patients a month
trials <- tite_boin12_simulate(
  target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25,
  p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
  p_resp = c(0.20, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.38),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, window = 45, resp_window = 60,
  accrual_rate = 3 / 30, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated TITE-BOIN12 trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   doses                : 5
#>   DLT limit            : 0.35
#>   response limit       : 0.25
#>   cohorts              : 12 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 36
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                     DL1   DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5
#> Patients treated   7.17 12.18 8.30 5.70 2.65
#> DLTs observed      0.41  1.33 2.19 2.02 1.35
#> Responses observed 1.31  4.36 2.93 2.15 1.04
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#> max_cohorts 
#>         100 
#> 
#> Average trial duration: 565.4
summary(trials$duration)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   454.4   538.7   565.7   565.4   592.8   667.0
